title: Rice and Peas
subtitle: Jamaican coconut rice with kidney beans
excerpt: Rice and peas is the cornerstone side dish of Jamaican cooking, served at Sunday dinners and celebrations across the island. Long-grain rice is simmered in coconut milk with kidney beans, spring onions, thyme, and allspice until fluffy and fragrant. The name is slightly misleading: the peas are in fact kidney beans, a distinction that catches out many first-time cooks.
sourceNotes: Rice and peas is a Sunday staple throughout Jamaica and the wider Caribbean diaspora. The dish draws on both African culinary traditions brought to the island during the slave trade and the pantry staples that defined Caribbean cooking for generations.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Reheat with a splash of water.

content.text: The secret to perfect rice and peas is the liquid ratio: coconut milk and stock together give the rice a richness and depth that water alone cannot. Rinse the rice thoroughly before cooking to remove excess starch, which would otherwise make the finished dish sticky and clumped. To make this vegan, substitute the chicken stock with vegetable stock.

content.text: Rinse the long-grain rice in several changes of cold water until the water runs clear. Drain well in a sieve.
Pour the coconut milk and chicken stock into a large saucepan and bring to the boil over medium-high heat. Add the spring onions, garlic, thyme sprigs, and allspice.
Add the drained kidney beans to the pan and stir to combine. Season generously with salt.
Add the rinsed rice and stir once to distribute everything evenly. Bring back to the boil, then reduce the heat to its lowest setting.
Cover the pan tightly with a lid and cook for 20 to 25 minutes without lifting the lid. The steam trapped inside is what cooks the rice evenly. Resist the urge to stir or check on it.
After 20 minutes, check if the liquid has been absorbed and the rice is tender with a slight bite. If there is still liquid remaining, replace the lid and cook for a further 3 to 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat and leave to steam with the lid on for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork, remove the spring onion stalks and thyme sprigs, and serve alongside jerk chicken or any grilled meat.

items.symptom: The rice is mushy and clumped together
items.cause: The rice was not rinsed before cooking, causing excess starch to create a sticky texture. The heat may also have been too high.
items.fix: Always rinse rice until the water runs clear. Keep the heat at its lowest once the pan is covered. If the rice is already cooked and sticky, spread it on a tray and leave uncovered for a few minutes to dry out.

items.symptom: The rice is undercooked and still has crunch in the centre
items.cause: The liquid ratio was not quite right, or the lid was lifted during cooking, letting steam escape.
items.fix: Add a small splash of boiling water (2 to 3 tablespoons), replace the lid, and continue cooking for 5 more minutes on a very low heat. Do not lift the lid again until the time is up.

items.symptom: The rice is scorched on the bottom of the pan
items.cause: The heat was too high once the liquid began to absorb, or the pan is too thin to distribute heat evenly.
items.fix: Use a heavy-bottomed saucepan and keep the heat very low once the lid goes on. A scorched bottom is common in thin pans; a heat diffuser mat can help. Scrape out and serve the unscorched rice above.
